clue.text: Unusual for us to gossip

parts.note: rum is an informal British word for odd or strange
something for us is ours, the possessive our

explanation.surface: Someone finds it odd that people are spreading tittle-tattle about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip and hearsay are synonyms: idle talk passed between people.

clue.text: Sharp pains produced by needles

definitions.meaning: a stitch is a sudden sharp pain in the side, as when running
loops of thread made by sewing or knitting needles

explanation.surface: Someone complains of sharp pains caused by injections.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: side pains from exertion, and the loops a sewing or knitting needle makes.

clue.text: It is included in a doctor's rounds

indicators.note: the word it sits inside the letters for a doctor's, as something included

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree, with S for the possessive
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something is part of a physician's hospital rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambit is a range or circuit of action, so plural circuits or spheres are rounds.

clue.text: Horace set about female — his main opponent?

indicators.note: the rearranged name goes around the letter for female
the letters of the name Horace are set out afresh in another order

explanation.surface: A man named Horace attacked a woman: is he his chief enemy?
explanation.definitionFit: A chief enemy or principal adversary is one's greatest opponent.

clue.text: New act with hat and stick

indicators.note: new signals the letters of act and hat made into something fresh

explanation.surface: A performer has a new routine with a hat and a cane.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick something on is to fasten or fix it, a synonym.

clue.text: Of course, there's no choice with these

definitions.text: Of course, there's no choice with these

parts.words: Of course, there's no choice with these
parts.note: a fixed-price restaurant menu offers no choice of dish at each course

explanation.surface: Naturally, these leave you no options.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed menus at a restaurant serve each course without alternatives for the diner.

clue.text: Routine disguise for army scout

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so the letters of army scout are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scout wears a disguise as part of normal army practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Routine and habitual mean the same: done as usual.

clue.text: Wrest apart and scatter

indicators.note: pulled apart, the letters of wrest are separated and reassembled

explanation.surface: Wrench something apart and fling the pieces about.
explanation.definitionFit: To scatter things over a surface is a synonym.

clue.text: Keep dark for a set period

parts.note: a keep is the stronghold of a castle, so a fort
the dark of the day is night

explanation.surface: Stay in the dark for a fixed length of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Fourteen days is a fixed span of time, a set period.

clue.text: Drink brought back by mother from holiday resort

indicators.note: the word for drink is turned to run the other way

parts.note: to lap is to drink like a cat
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Mum brings home a bottle from her trip abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: PALMA is the capital of Majorca, a Spanish island popular with tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: The Majorcan capital is a popular Mediterranean destination for tourists.

clue.text: He goes down or rises as the star

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word or is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A stage performer either falls or climbs as the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes down' places HE first in this down answer; 'rises' turns OR to RO beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a film or story is its hero, the lead role.

clue.text: Search frantically for means of support

indicators.note: a frantic movement jumbles the letters of search

explanation.surface: Hunting desperately for a source of income.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch is a curved structure that supports a bridge or building above it.

clue.text: Business expense that has gone up?

definitions.meaning: a firm's running costs such as rent and heating
something gone up is above one's head, in the sky

explanation.surface: A company cost that has risen.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed running costs of a firm; and an adverb for above, aloft.

clue.text: Unscrupulous person retiring to rest, perhaps

parts.note: a retiring person is reserved or bashful

indicators.note: perhaps shows that rest is only one arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A crook going off to bed for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is a dishonest person, especially a lawyer, who uses sharp practice.

clue.text: Robin to indicate complicity in trick

parts.note: Robin Hood is the English outlaw of legend
a wink signals a shared secret

explanation.surface: Robin gives a knowing wink as part of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To deceive or dupe someone is to trick them.

clue.text: See key goes to the agent

parts.note: E is a musical key
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: Look, the key goes to the secret agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch sight of something is to see it.

clue.text: Study exam question

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: Reading over an exam paper's question.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute or challenge something is to question it.

clue.text: Novel is remote and tedious

indicators.note: novel as an adjective means new, so the letters of is remote are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A book set somewhere far away is dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Tedious and wearisome are synonyms: boring.

clue.text: Old soldier — there could be a few neater characters

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a few

indicators.note: signals that the letters could form another word when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An ex-serviceman might have a tidier character.
explanation.definitionFit: A veteran is someone who served long in the armed forces.

clue.text: Firm left to slip into bankruptcy?

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm
a lapse is a slip or error

explanation.surface: A company left to fall into insolvency.
explanation.definitionFit: Business failure or ruin; the question mark admits it's an example, not a synonym.

clue.text: Hardy, no: evergreen, yes

definitions.meaning: Stan ... was the partner of Oliver Hardy, so not Hardy himself
the ... or bay tree keeps its leaves all year

explanation.surface: A gardener says this plant isn't frost-tolerant but does keep its leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like a gardening word for frost-tolerant, but points to the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: One half of a famous comedy duo; also a bay tree that keeps its leaves.

clue.text: This French rebel is a red

parts.note: ce is French for this
to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: This French revolutionary is a communist.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry red is a shade of the colour red.

clue.text: A good conductor works on the beat

definitions.meaning: a police officer walks a beat

explanation.surface: An orchestral conductor who keeps time well.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal that conducts electricity; also slang for a police officer.

clue.text: Times of enchantment

definitions.meaning: magic charms; singular noun, the answer is the plural charms

explanation.surface: Periods of magic.
explanation.definitionFit: Short periods of time; also magic incantations.

clue.text: Legitimate student expelled with dire result

indicators.note: an expelled student is sent out, so the letter for student goes

parts.note: lawful means legitimate
L is a learner, a student driver

explanation.surface: A rightful pupil is thrown out, with terrible results.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire and terrible are synonyms.

clue.text: Clerk to confine drug pedlar

parts.note: to pen is to shut in
a pusher sells illegal drugs

explanation.surface: An office worker locks up a drug dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen-pusher is a derogatory term for an office clerk.

clue.text: Finger the back of a book

definitions.meaning: the alphabetical list at the end of a book

explanation.surface: Point at the back cover of a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The forefinger; also the alphabetical listing at the end of a book.

clue.text: Complain loudly about schooltime left — it may be grinding

indicators.note: the word for complaining loudly goes around the school period

parts.note: to wail is to cry out in complaint
a term is a period of the school year

explanation.surface: A child moans about school having left them grinding away at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill driven by water grinds grain, so it may be grinding.
